newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Megawati appeal to take six months.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Megawati appeal to take six months.

text.p: A lawyer for ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri said on Saturday it would be six months before an appeal against dismissal of her case against government and party rivals is decided.

Megawati's chief lawyer R.O. Tambunan told Reuters he had lodged an appeal with the Jakarta High Court on Friday after judges in the Central Jakarta State Court said on Thursday they did not have the authority to hear Megawati's case.
"It will be about six months before there is a decision. There will be no hearing as the High Court does not have hearings," Tambunan said.

Megawati sued Surjadi, the government-backed Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) chief, his supporters, armed forces chief General Fiesal Tanjung, Interior Minister Yogie Memet and national police chief Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo for backing a congress in June at which she was ousted.
She argued the congress was illegal and asked the court to rule against it, but the judges accepted the defence arguments that the issue was an internal party matter.

The court also agreed with arguments put forward by the government and military lawyers that their clients were just carrying out their duties to support political development and provide security in supporting the congress.
"We have appealed to the High Court so that it can order the State Court to hear that case again," Tambunan said.

Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights said on Saturday that government interference in the internal party affairs of the PDI was behind the riots in the capital on July 27 this year in which at least five people died.
